WINTER COLOR BY
MUSIC SYMBOL
Dynamics · Tempo terms · Music symbols — 3 levels with answer keys
Grades 2–5 · 27 worksheets · 27 answer keys

Teacher Notes

Winter Color by Music Symbol · 3 levels · grades 2–5

How to use

  • Pick a level for each student or group, print the worksheets single-sided, and hand out crayons or colored pencils.
  • Students read the marking in each space, find what it means in the color key, and color the space. Every space has a marking in it.
  • White in a key means leave the space white. Gray can be a gray crayon or a light pencil shade.
  • Check with the answer key that follows each level. Keys are full-color pages you can print or project.
  • All three levels use the same nine winter pictures, so one class can color the same picture at three different reading levels.

Great for

  • Early finishers and music centers
  • Sub plans (the answer keys and reference page make it no-prep)
  • A quick check of dynamics, tempo and symbols before a winter concert

Level guide

LevelSkillSuggestedPages
Level ADynamicsGrades 2–34–12 worksheets, 13–21 keys
Level BTempo termsGrades 3–522–30 worksheets, 31–39 keys
Level CMusic symbolsGrades 4–540–48 worksheets, 49–57 keys

Level A: pp, p, mp, mf, f, ff (the key gives the meaning, such as very soft or medium loud). Level B: largo, adagio, andante, moderato, allegro, presto (the key gives the meaning, such as slow or fast). Level C: fermata, repeat sign, crescendo, decrescendo, staccato, accent, slur (the key gives the name). Each picture uses up to five colors, so each key shows up to five of the markings.

Standards

Practices music vocabulary and reading notation: dynamics, tempo and expressive symbols. Supports the National Core Arts Standards for Music, Responding (MU:Re7.2) and Performing (MU:Pr4.3), grades 2–5. Keep claims modest: this is a practice activity.

What’s inside

Page 3: student reference (every marking and its meaning). Level A: pages 4–12 worksheets, 13–21 keys; Level B: pages 22–30 worksheets, 31–39 keys; Level C: pages 40–48 worksheets, 49–57 keys. Last page: terms of use and credits. Pictures: 1. Snowman, 2. Mittens, 3. Penguin, 4. Cocoa Mug, 5. Igloo, 6. Snowflake, 7. Snowy Pine Tree, 8. Winter Hat, 9. Ice Skate.

No songs, lyrics or copyrighted characters are used. All pictures are original line art.

Student Reference

Keep this page nearby while you color.

Level A · Dynamics

MarkingNameMeans
pp · pianissimovery soft
p · pianosoft
mp · mezzo pianomedium soft
mf · mezzo fortemedium loud
f · forteloud
ff · fortissimovery loud

Level B · Tempo terms

TermNameMeans
largovery slow, broad
adagioslow and calm
andanteat a walking pace
moderatoa medium speed
allegrofast and lively
prestovery fast

Level C · Music symbols

SymbolNameMeans
fermatahold the note longer
repeat signplay the music again
crescendoget louder
decrescendoget softer
staccatoshort and detached
accentplay the note stronger
slursmooth and connected

Dynamics: m stands for mezzo (medium). A crescendo and a decrescendo change the dynamic gradually; a staccato dot goes on the notehead side, an accent goes over or under the note, and a slur joins notes of different pitches.
